title: Reiteration raises force: partial overruling of the T-344 R-2 framing
subject: reiteration-force
ratio:
Reiteration is a first-class force-raising mechanism at every tier, computed on read from the
citation index (addendum section 5: jurisprudencia constante; Llewellyn's accumulating
citations): a tier 1-3 record with three or more qualifying consistent applications (the C
counter) computes force `settled`, above plain `binding`; a tier-4 record with three or more
computes force `reiterated`, above plain `persuasive`. A never-recited ratio may decay to
persuasive (flagged only, never auto-expired).

PRESERVED, explicitly, against a different error than the one T-344's R-2 framing guarded
against: T-344's own argument -- that any N>1 threshold is a de facto ban on binding -- is
PRESERVED and UNTOUCHED, because this record does not require N>1 for ANY bindingness.
`authority_tier` (1-4) remains the ISSUANCE authority, unchanged: how much adversarial process a
decision survived at birth. A single verdicted decision still binds at issuance; no N>1 threshold
is required to bind. What changes is the CEILING a ratio's force may reach through accumulated,
consistent, unforced application -- never the FLOOR of what makes a decision bind in the first
place.

R-3's zeroing rule (a recognized contrary application zeroes the counter, never merely skips an
increment) and R-2's disclosed N=3 threshold (with its bracket: Mexico's five, Spain's historical
two) are carried forward as the reiteration mechanism's own terms. The candidate-surfacing job
R-2's flag performed survives as a side effect (a `reiterated` tier-4 record is exactly the
promotion candidate R-2 wanted surfaced) but is no longer the flag's whole meaning.

This is a partial overruling of the T-344 R-2 framing ("repeated confirmation becomes a separate,
non-binding reiterated flag on tier-4 records -- not a replacement of tier 3 and not a new
binding tier"): the framing correctly read the materials T-344 had at the time, and is not
declared erroneous ab initio; it is superseded, forward-looking, by new operator-supplied
doctrine (the addendum), on the reasoning stated above and in the accompanying factor note.
scope_conditions: any agent computing, rendering, or citing a record's force
revisit_trigger: Revisit if measured registry velocity makes C>=3 unreachable across two consecutive epics, or if a recorded amendment changes the force enum

relations.factor_note:
doctrinal_change: the addendum's graded-force doctrine is new external doctrine that changes the
applicable rule; it is not a claim that T-344's own reasoning was defective at the time it was
written. The addendum (Sandoval Islas, "Distinciones entre la interpretacion de disposiciones
legislativas y la interpretacion de precedentes," Problema 20, IIJ-UNAM 2026, DOI
10.22201/iij.24487937e.2026.20.20316, section 5) states: "Reiteration raises force (jurisprudencia
constante ... a ratio's force level increases with N consistent applications across sessions,
recorded via the citation index)." Its own instruction line prevails over prior assumptions where
it conflicts with them: "Where this addendum conflicts with prior assumptions in the roadmap,
this addendum prevails."

T-344 reasoned correctly from the materials it had: its central argument -- that any N>1
threshold is a de facto ban on binding, because it would let a first, isolated decision escape
ever binding at all -- is expressly PRESERVED here. This record does not impose an N>1 requirement
on bindingness at any tier. `authority_tier` remains untouched as the issuance-authority axis; a
single verdicted decision still binds at issuance with no reiteration required. What the new
doctrine changes is the ceiling a ratio's force may reach through consistent, unforced, repeated
application -- not the floor T-344 was defending.

The overruling is therefore forward-looking, on new operator-supplied doctrine (a
`determination` choosing which reading controls now), not a corrective act claiming R-2 was
erroneous ab initio. Coordinator decision A2 (.harness/coordinator-decisions-addendum.md)
explicitly directs this reasoning "to be published as a formal record."

validity_conditions: force is computed on read by precedent.py; no stored force field exists
